newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, gold down, silver up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, gold down, silver up.

text.p: COMEX gold futures ended lower but other New York precious metals futures ended higher Monday on light volume.

"Gold opened offered with the dollar sharply higher but then we saw a little shortcovering, while platinum and palladium were up, helped by news from Russia," Credit Lyonnais Rouse chief bullion dealer Scott Mehlman said.
COMEX June gold ended down $0.60 at $351.00 an ounce after dipping to an early low at $349.40 on some trade selling which was met by some fund buying, COMEX locals said.
Hourly momentum indicators were beginning to turn positive again, but on a daily basis June gold has remained locked in a $350 to $355 range for a month, analysts noted.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $348.00/50 against the London afternoon fix of $349.00 and Friday's New York close of $348.50/$349.00.
The dollar jumped to a new four-year high against yen and to a three-week high against mark early Monday, helping U.S. bonds and stocks to recover some ground too.
But the jump in the dollar/yen rate pushed gold in yen back up to around 43,800 yen an ounce, its highest level for nearly a year.
Gold demand in Japan last year fell 41 percent, partly as a result of the weak yen and high yen gold price.
Meanwhile, in the U.S., gold jewelry demand continues to sustain the physical market, with total sales rising to $12.3 billion in 1996 from $9.9 billion in 1992, according to the World Gold Council.

U.S. TV shopping channel QVC led the rise in gold jewelery sales last year, with a 14 percent gain to $450 million and is now the largest 18-karat gold jewelry retailer in the U.S. and the largest 14-karat jewelry retailer in the world.
Gold was weaker than silver though Monday, with spot gold/silver ratio slipping to 72.6 from 73.5 Friday, after recovering steadily in March from a 22-month low at 65.6.
COMEX May silver closed up 4.8 cent Monday at $4.785, continuing its recovery from last Thursday's contract low of $4.655.
After becoming oversold last week, some speculative shortcovering was occurring, while fabrication demand for silver was said to be good at levels under $5.00 an ounce, traders said.
July platinum ended up $3.70 at $368.00, with June palladium up $3.50 at $153.25.
Monday, a Russian trade representative to Japan said there will be no Russian supplies of PGMs to Japan in April and May's supplies are also in doubt.
Russian PGM exports would also be much lower in 1997 than in 1996, he added.
The latest round of annual Russian-Japanese talks on PGM supplies, usually held in December, were postponed indefinitely, due to Russian fiscal and administrative problems.
Russian exports account for about 60 percent of world palladium supplies.
